ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small ball with mass $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is thrown horizontally from a height $h=5\mathrm{m}$ above the ground with an initial horizontal velocity $\v_{O}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. Air resistance is neglected, and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Find the momentum increment $\Delta p$ of the ball during the projectile motion.
2. Find the momentum $p^{\prime}$ of the ball when it hits the ground.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$10\mathrm{kg\cdotm/s}$
$10\sqrt{2}\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}$; the direction is at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small ball with mass $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is thrown horizontally from a height $h=5\mathrm{m}$ above the ground with an initial horizontal velocity $\v_{O}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. Air resistance is neglected, and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. Find the momentum increment $\Delta p$ of the ball during the projectile motion. 2. Find the momentum $p^{\prime}$ of the ball when it hits the ground.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: $10\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}$ $10\sqrt{2}\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}$; the direction is at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given m = 1 kg, h = 5 m, initial horizontal velocity v0 = 10 m/s, g = 10 m/s^2, and no air resistance. Because the ball is thrown horizontally, its initial vertical velocity is 0. The fall time is found from h = (1/2)gt^2: 5 = (1/2)(10)t^2 = 5t^2, so t = 1 s. During flight, the only force is gravity, so the momentum increment equals the impulse of gravity: Δp = mgt = (1)(10)(1) = 10 kg·m/s downward. The horizontal momentum stays constant: px = mv0 = (1)(10) = 10 kg·m/s. The final vertical momentum is py = mgt = 10 kg·m/s downward. Therefore the final momentum magnitude is p' = sqrt(px^2 + py^2) = sqrt(10^2 + 10^2) = 10√2 kg·m/s. Since tan θ = py/px = 1, the direction is 45° below the horizontal.
